- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment drops sharply post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward; if <10% below, adjust upward — especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Horizon-specific: 10–15 day forecasts often overestimate; 20+ day forecasts underperform — adjust downward for longer horizons if sentiment is weak or volatile.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (e.g., 3+ consecutive), model tends to ignore sentiment and overreact to recent price — apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to forecast.
